'''Yaiza Canzani García''' is a Spanish and Uruguayan mathematician known for her work in [[mathematical analysis]], and particularly in [[spectral geometry]] and [[microlocal analysis]]. She is an associate professor of mathematics at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]].{{r|uncsad}}

==Education and career==
Canzani was born in Spain and grew up in Uruguay.{{r|lathisms}} She was an undergraduate at the [[University of the Republic (Uruguay)]], where she earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics in 2008.{{r|cv}} She completed a Ph.D. in 2013 at [[McGill University]] in [[Montreal]], Canada, with the dissertation ''Spectral Geometry of Conformally Covariant Operators'' jointly supervised by Dmitry Jakobson and John Toth.{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral study at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and as a [[Benjamin Peirce]] Fellow at [[Harvard University]], she became an assistant professor of mathematics at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2016.{{r|cv}} In 2021 she was promoted to associate professor.{{r|cv|uncsad}}

==Recognition==
Canzani is a recipient of a [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|National Science Foundation CAREER Award]] and a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]].{{r|cv|awmsad}} She is the 2022 winner of the [[Sadosky Prize]] in analysis of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].{{r|uncsad|awmsad}} The award was given "in recognition of outstanding contributions in spectral geometry and microlocal analysis", citing her "breakthrough results on nodal sets, random waves, Weyl Laws, <math>L^p</math>-norms, and other problems on eigenfunctions and eigenvalues on [[Riemannian manifold]]s".{{r|awmsad}}

She was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]], in the 2025 class of fellows.{{r|fams}}
